17	#   refused_peak_hours   | LEADV2_DISPATCH_REFUSED: peak_hours
18	#   refused_quota        | LEADV2_DISPATCH_REFUSED: <other marker>, GLM REROUTE, or rc 75
19	#   refused_channel_down | rc 77 (probe/run channel-down admission, e.g. kimi-coder.sh)
20	#   ran                  | not a refusal -- the arm ran (well or badly); rc/output still
21	#                           need the caller's own provider_error/empty_response/
22	#                           no_verdict_marker classification, never assumed here.

44	  fi

46	  # Compatibility only for older GLM quota gates that predate the explicit marker.

54	  # provider error, per the existing kimi rc-75 contract (KIMI-CHANNEL-01b).

443	  if [[ -n "${PARSED_VERDICT}" ]]; then

447	    [[ -n "${PARSED_VERDICT}" ]] && VERDICT_SOURCE="alt_marker"

451	  # MAJOR fix (review-verdict.md dispatch-product-close.sh:49-56): REVIEW_FINDINGS
452	  # used to be optional -- a reviewer emitting only REVIEW_VERDICT: PASS was

454	  # exactly one valid findings-count marker (none = unscoped verdict; more than

2	# tests/test-review-silence-gate.sh — N-5: the review channel must fail loudly, never
3	# silently. Regression coverage for the four defects fixed in
4	# leadv2-dispatch-product-close.sh (D1 refusal-exits-0, D3 no-artifact-guarantee, D4
5	# one-reason-for-four-causes, D5 kimi-only refusal fallback).
6	#
7	# Drives the REAL leadv2-dispatch-product-close.sh end to end (never a reimplementation
8	# of its logic). Each scenario gets its own throwaway git repo (fixture root) so diffs,
9	# review-ledger dedup, and close-owner pidfiles never collide across scenarios. The
10	# resolver is stubbed via LEADV2_GLM_POLICY_RESOLVER (a tiny python3 script -- the real
11	# resolver is invoked with `python3 "$resolver" ...`, so the stub must be valid python,
12	# not bash) and reviewer arms are stubbed via the existing injection points
13	# (LEADV2_DISPATCH_GLM_BIN, LEADV2_DISPATCH_ARCHITECT_BIN).
14	#
15	# Run directly, assert $? inline -- no wrapper that swallows the exit code.
16	# Run: bash scripts/tests/test-review-silence-gate.sh
17	# Exit 0 = all pass; non-zero = failures found.

45	# make_fixture_root <name> <unique-content> -> prints the repo path on stdout.

    if ! grep -q '^[[:space:]]*REVIEW_VERDICT:' "${review_out}" 2>/dev/null && [[ "${_pc_body_bytes}" -lt "${_pc_body_min}" ]]; then
      # Evidence-of-real-output: non-empty stderr or a cost-recorded line in it.
      if [[ -s "${review_err}" ]] || grep -q 'cost recorded:' "${review_err}" 2>/dev/null; then
        printf 'status: blocked\nreason: review_body_lost\narm: %s\n' "${reviewer}" > "${HANDOFF}/review-gate.md"
        emit decision "review_gate task=${TASK} status=blocked reason=review_body_lost arm=${reviewer}"
        _dl_note dead review_body_lost "arm=${reviewer} bytes=${_pc_body_bytes}"
        _stamp_review_terminal blocked
        exit 6
      fi
    fi
  fi

  # ARM-NO-VERDICT-01 (dispatch-4fb7381a): a reviewer that runs to completion (cls==
  # "ran", not a refusal, and not review_body_lost -- that guard above already exited
  # on the one case with positive evidence of lost spend) but produces output the gate
  # cannot use -- a provider error, sub-floor/empty output, or real prose with no
  # REVIEW_VERDICT: marker (e.g. a transcript ending in "[Tool use interrupted]") -- is
  # EXACTLY as much "this arm produced nothing usable" as a refused_* arm. The pool
  # resolver already ordered 3-5 quota-eligible arms for this task; killing the lane on
  # the FIRST arm's truncation when others were resolved and available (lane 4fb7381a,
  # 2026-08-07: reviewer=kimi, pool_n=5, dead on arm #1) is the defect this block fixes.
  # Same tried[]/next_ok_arm_after bookkeeping as the refused_* branch above; only the
  # reason vocabulary (provider_error/empty_response/no_verdict_marker) differs, and it
  # is preserved verbatim from the pre-fallthrough N-5 D4 split below.
  resolve_review_artifact || true
  review_file="${REVIEW_ARTIFACT:-${review_out}}"
  _pc_no_verdict_reason=""
  if [[ ${review_rc} -ne 0 && -z "${REVIEW_ARTIFACT}" ]]; then
    _pc_no_verdict_reason="provider_error"
  elif [[ ! -s "${review_file}" ]] || ! review_floor_ok "${review_file}"; then
    _pc_no_verdict_reason="empty_response"
  elif ! parse_review_verdict "${review_file}"; then
    _pc_no_verdict_reason="no_verdict_marker"
  fi

  if [[ -n "${_pc_no_verdict_reason}" ]]; then
    _pc_tried_csv="$(IFS=,; echo "${PC_TRIED[*]:-}")"
    _pc_remaining="$(_pc_remaining_ok_after "${reviewer}")"
    emit decision "review_gate task=${TASK} status=arm_no_verdict arm=${reviewer} reason=${_pc_no_verdict_reason} tried=${_pc_tried_csv} remaining=${_pc_remaining}"
    if [[ ${#PC_TRIED[@]} -ge 4 ]]; then
      _pc_unavailable=1
      _pc_exhaust_kind="no_verdict"
      break
    fi
    next_arm="$(next_ok_arm_after "${reviewer}" || true)"
    if [[ -z "${next_arm}" || "${next_arm}" == "${AUTHOR}" ]]; then
      _pc_unavailable=1
      _pc_exhaust_kind="no_verdict"
      break
    fi
    reviewer="${next_arm}"
    continue
  fi

  break
done
if [[ "${_pc_unavailable}" == "1" ]]; then
  _pc_tried_csv="$(IFS=,; echo "${PC_TRIED[*]:-}")"
  if [[ "${_pc_exhaust_kind}" == "no_verdict" ]]; then
    # Pool genuinely exhausted -- every arm ran but produced nothing usable. Keep the
    # SAME terminal cause (no_verdict_marker) the pre-fallthrough code used for this
    # exit path so downstream terminal-state consumers see no behaviour change for the
    # exhausted case, only the new per-arm arm_no_verdict lines and the full tried= list
    # attached to the death itself (dispatch-4fb7381a: reviewer never advanced past
    # kimi, so tried= could only ever show one name -- this is the fix's proof).
    printf 'status: blocked\nreason: no_verdict_marker\n' > "${HANDOFF}/review-gate.md"
    emit decision "review_gate task=${TASK} status=blocked reason=no_verdict_marker tried=${_pc_tried_csv}"
    _dl_note dead no_verdict_marker "tried=${_pc_tried_csv}"
    _stamp_review_terminal blocked
    exit 6
  fi
  _pc_refusal="${refusal:-all_arms_unavailable}"
  _pc_write_unreviewed "${_pc_refusal}" "${pool}" "${_pc_tried_csv}" "${resolver_rc}" "${resolver_stderr}"
  exit 9
fi

input.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# tests/test-review-arm-no-verdict.sh — ARM-NO-VERDICT-01 (dispatch-4fb7381a): a
# reviewer arm that runs to completion but produces nothing usable (no REVIEW_VERDICT:
# marker, truncated/empty output, or a provider error) must fall through to the NEXT
# arm in the resolved pool -- reusing the existing tried[]/next_ok_arm_after
# bookkeeping -- exactly like a refused_* arm already does. Only when the whole pool
# is exhausted does the lane die, with reason=no_verdict_marker and the FULL tried=
# list attached.
#
# Regression coverage for the 2026-08-07 incident: lane 4fb7381a resolved a 5-arm
# review pool (`review_pool_resolve rc=0 reviewer=kimi pool_n=5`), kimi's own transcript
# ended in "[Tool use interrupted]" with no verdict marker, and the lane was killed on
# THAT FIRST arm -- `review_gate status=blocked reason=no_verdict_marker` /
# `dispatch_terminal terminal=dead cause=no_verdict_marker` -- without ever trying the
# other 4 resolved arms.
#
# Drives the REAL leadv2-dispatch-product-close.sh end to end, same harness pattern as
# test-review-silence-gate.sh (stub resolver + stub reviewer launchers, never a
# reimplementation of the gate's own logic).
#
# Run: bash scripts/tests/test-review-arm-no-verdict.sh

set -uo pipefail
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
SCRIPTS_ROOT="$(cd "${SCRIPT_DIR}/.." && pwd)"
source "${SCRIPTS_ROOT}/leadv2-temp.sh"

PRODUCT_CLOSE_SH="${SCRIPTS_ROOT}/leadv2-dispatch-product-close.sh"

PASS=0; FAIL=0; ERRORS=()
log()  { printf -- '[TEST] %s\n' "$*"; }
pass() { PASS=$((PASS + 1)); log "PASS: $1"; }
fail() { FAIL=$((FAIL + 1)); ERRORS+=("FAIL: $1"); log "FAIL: $1"; }

SUITE_TMP="$(lv2_mktemp_dir "review-arm-no-verdict-test")"
trap 'rm -rf "$SUITE_TMP"' EXIT

make_fixture_root() {
  local name="$1" content="$2"
  local repo="${SUITE_TMP}/${name}/root"
  mkdir -p "$repo"
  git -C "$repo" init -q
  git -C "$repo" config user.email "test@test.local"
  git -C "$repo" config user.name "test"
  printf 'baseline\n' > "$repo/file.txt"
  git -C "$repo" add file.txt
  git -C "$repo" commit -q -m init
  lv2_assert_scratch_repo "$repo"
  printf '%s\n' "$content" >> "$repo/file.txt"
  printf '%s' "$repo"
}

make_resolver_stub() {
  local name="$1" reviewer="$2" pool="$3"
  local stub="${SUITE_TMP}/${name}/resolver.py"
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$stub")"
  cat > "$stub" <<PY
print("reviewer=${reviewer}")
print("pool=${pool}")
print("refusal=")
PY
  printf '%s' "$stub"
}

# make_glm_stub <name> <mode> -> prints the stub path on stdout.
#   pass       - clean REVIEW_VERDICT: PASS
#   no_verdict - >200 bytes / >=3 lines of real prose, NO REVIEW_VERDICT: marker (rc 0)
#   empty      - writes nothing at all (rc 0)
make_glm_stub() {
  local name="$1" mode="$2"
  local stub="${SUITE_TMP}/${name}/glm-stub.sh"
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$stub")"
  cat > "$stub" <<'SH'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
outfile=""
args=("$@")
i=0
while [[ $i -lt ${#args[@]} ]]; do
  if [[ "${args[$i]}" == "--out" ]]; then
    outfile="${args[$((i+1))]}"
  fi
  i=$((i+1))
done
SH
  case "$mode" in
    pass)
      cat >> "$stub" <<'SH'
printf 'REVIEW_VERDICT: PASS\nREVIEW_FINDINGS: critical=0 high=0 medium=0 low=0\nClean diff, no issues found by the stub reviewer arm.\n' > "$outfile"
exit 0
SH
      ;;
    no_verdict)
      cat >> "$stub" <<'SH'
printf 'Reviewing the diff now, this looks like a reasonable change overall.\nStill going through the files one by one to check for edge cases.\n[Tool use interrupted]\n' > "$outfile"
exit 0
SH
      ;;
    empty)
      cat >> "$stub" <<'SH'
: > "$outfile"
exit 0
SH
      ;;
  esac
  chmod +x "$stub"
  printf '%s' "$stub"
}

# make_arch_stub <name> <mode> -> prints the stub path on stdout (drives the sonnet/
# opus branch of run_reviewer_arm, whose launcher writes to stdout, redirected by the
# caller into review_out).
#   pass       - clean REVIEW_VERDICT: PASS
#   no_verdict - >200 bytes / >=3 lines of real prose, NO REVIEW_VERDICT: marker (rc 0)
#   empty      - writes nothing at all (rc 0)
make_arch_stub() {
  local name="$1" mode="$2"
  local stub="${SUITE_TMP}/${name}/arch-stub.sh"
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$stub")"
  case "$mode" in
    pass)
      printf '#!/usr/bin/env bash\nprintf "REVIEW_VERDICT: PASS\\nREVIEW_FINDINGS: critical=0 high=0 medium=0 low=0\\nAll good, reviewed thoroughly, nothing to flag in this diff.\\n"\nexit 0\n' > "$stub"
      ;;
    no_verdict)
      printf '#!/usr/bin/env bash\nprintf "Reviewing the diff now, this looks like a reasonable change overall.\\nStill going through the files one by one to check for edge cases in this review.\\n[Tool use interrupted]\\n"\nexit 0\n' > "$stub"
      ;;
    empty)
      printf '#!/usr/bin/env bash\nexit 0\n' > "$stub"
      ;;
  esac
  chmod +x "$stub"
  printf '%s' "$stub"
}

run_close() { # <root> <sig8> <author> <resolver>
  local root="$1" sig8="$2" author="$3" resolver="$4"
  local cache="${SUITE_TMP}/${sig8}/cache"
  mkdir -p "$cache"
  LEADV2_GLM_POLICY_RESOLVER="$resolver" \
  LEADV2_DISPATCH_CACHE_DIR="$cache" \
  LEADV2_JOURNAL_BIN=/bin/true \
  LEADV2_E2E_OWNERSHIP=0 \
    bash "$PRODUCT_CLOSE_SH" "$root" "$sig8" "$author" "" 0 1 "" 2>&1
}

# ── Test 1 (RED against pre-fix code): first arm no-verdict -> second arm invoked and
#    ITS verdict is what gets recorded. reviewer=sonnet (arch stub, no_verdict) falls
#    through to glm (glm stub, pass).
root1="$(make_fixture_root t1 "t1-unique-diff-content")"
resolver1="$(make_resolver_stub t1 sonnet "sonnet:ok:,glm:ok:")"
arch1="$(make_arch_stub t1 no_verdict)"
glm1="$(make_glm_stub t1 pass)"
out1="$(LEADV2_DISPATCH_ARCHITECT_BIN="$arch1" LEADV2_DISPATCH_GLM_BIN="$glm1" run_close "$root1" t1sig001 codex "$resolver1")"; rc1=$?
gate1="${root1}/docs/handoff/dispatch-t1sig001/review-gate.md"
if [[ $rc1 -eq 0 ]]; then pass "Test 1 (fallthrough_to_second_arm): exit 0"; else fail "Test 1: expected exit 0, got ${rc1} -- ${out1}"; fi
if [[ -f "$gate1" ]] && grep -q '^status: pass$' "$gate1"; then
  pass "Test 1: review-gate.md status=pass -- second arm's PASS verdict was recorded"
else
  fail "Test 1: review-gate.md wrong -- $(cat "$gate1" 2>/dev/null || echo MISSING)"
fi
if grep -q 'status=arm_no_verdict arm=sonnet reason=no_verdict_marker tried=sonnet remaining=1' <<<"$out1"; then
  pass "Test 1: journal carries arm_no_verdict arm=sonnet reason=no_verdict_marker tried=sonnet remaining=1"
else
  fail "Test 1: no arm_no_verdict fallthrough line for sonnet -- ${out1}"
fi
if grep -q 'status=ran author=codex reviewer=glm verdict=PASS' <<<"$out1"; then
  pass "Test 1: journal confirms the RECORDED verdict came from glm (the second arm), not sonnet"
else
  fail "Test 1: no ran/verdict=PASS line attributing the verdict to glm -- ${out1}"
fi

# ── Test 2: truncated/empty reviewer output is treated the SAME as no-verdict (falls
#    through), not treated as a pass. reviewer=sonnet (arch stub, empty) falls through
#    to glm (glm stub, pass).
root2="$(make_fixture_root t2 "t2-unique-diff-content")"
resolver2="$(make_resolver_stub t2 sonnet "sonnet:ok:,glm:ok:")"
arch2="$(make_arch_stub t2 empty)"
glm2="$(make_glm_stub t2 pass)"
out2="$(LEADV2_DISPATCH_ARCHITECT_BIN="$arch2" LEADV2_DISPATCH_GLM_BIN="$glm2" run_close "$root2" t2sig002 codex "$resolver2")"; rc2=$?
gate2="${root2}/docs/handoff/dispatch-t2sig002/review-gate.md"
if [[ $rc2 -eq 0 ]]; then pass "Test 2 (empty_output_falls_through): exit 0"; else fail "Test 2: expected exit 0, got ${rc2} -- ${out2}"; fi
if [[ -f "$gate2" ]] && grep -q '^status: pass$' "$gate2"; then
  pass "Test 2: review-gate.md status=pass -- empty first arm was NOT mistaken for a pass, glm's PASS was recorded instead"
else
  fail "Test 2: review-gate.md wrong -- $(cat "$gate2" 2>/dev/null || echo MISSING)"
fi
if grep -q 'status=arm_no_verdict arm=sonnet reason=empty_response tried=sonnet remaining=1' <<<"$out2"; then
  pass "Test 2: journal carries arm_no_verdict arm=sonnet reason=empty_response tried=sonnet remaining=1"
else
  fail "Test 2: no arm_no_verdict fallthrough line for empty sonnet output -- ${out2}"
fi

# ── Test 3: every arm in the pool returns no verdict -> the lane still dies with
#    no_verdict_marker AND the journal carries the FULL tried= list (both arms).
root3="$(make_fixture_root t3 "t3-unique-diff-content")"
resolver3="$(make_resolver_stub t3 sonnet "sonnet:ok:,glm:ok:")"
arch3="$(make_arch_stub t3 no_verdict)"
glm3="$(make_glm_stub t3 no_verdict)"
out3="$(LEADV2_DISPATCH_ARCHITECT_BIN="$arch3" LEADV2_DISPATCH_GLM_BIN="$glm3" run_close "$root3" t3sig003 codex "$resolver3")"; rc3=$?
gate3="${root3}/docs/handoff/dispatch-t3sig003/review-gate.md"
if [[ $rc3 -eq 6 ]]; then pass "Test 3 (pool_exhausted_dies): exit 6"; else fail "Test 3: expected exit 6, got ${rc3} -- ${out3}"; fi
if [[ -f "$gate3" ]] && grep -q '^status: blocked$' "$gate3" && grep -q '^reason: no_verdict_marker$' "$gate3"; then
  pass "Test 3: review-gate.md status=blocked reason=no_verdict_marker after both arms exhausted"
else
  fail "Test 3: review-gate.md wrong -- $(cat "$gate3" 2>/dev/null || echo MISSING)"
fi
if grep -q 'status=blocked reason=no_verdict_marker tried=sonnet,glm' <<<"$out3"; then
  pass "Test 3: terminal journal line carries FULL tried=sonnet,glm list"
else

if grep -q 'status=arm_no_verdict arm=sonnet reason=no_verdict_marker tried=sonnet remaining=1' <<<"$out3" \
  && grep -q 'status=arm_no_verdict arm=glm reason=no_verdict_marker tried=sonnet,glm remaining=0' <<<"$out3"; then
  pass "Test 3: both per-arm arm_no_verdict lines present with correct tried=/remaining="
else
  fail "Test 3: missing one or both per-arm arm_no_verdict lines -- ${out3}"
fi

# ── Test 4: a normal PASS on the first arm still invokes exactly ONE arm (no wasted
#    spend / no regression). glm's stub is wired to a mode that would fail loudly (via
#    review-gate.md contents) if ever invoked -- but the real proof is the absence of
#    review-glm.md/review-glm.err, since sonnet passing must never call run_reviewer_arm
#    a second time.
root4="$(make_fixture_root t4 "t4-unique-diff-content")"
resolver4="$(make_resolver_stub t4 sonnet "sonnet:ok:,glm:ok:")"
arch4="$(make_arch_stub t4 pass)"
glm4="$(make_glm_stub t4 no_verdict)"
out4="$(LEADV2_DISPATCH_ARCHITECT_BIN="$arch4" LEADV2_DISPATCH_GLM_BIN="$glm4" run_close "$root4" t4sig004 codex "$resolver4")"; rc4=$?
gate4="${root4}/docs/handoff/dispatch-t4sig004/review-gate.md"
glm4_out="${root4}/docs/handoff/dispatch-t4sig004/review-glm.md"
if [[ $rc4 -eq 0 ]]; then pass "Test 4 (first_arm_pass_no_waste): exit 0"; else fail "Test 4: expected exit 0, got ${rc4} -- ${out4}"; fi
if [[ -f "$gate4" ]] && grep -q '^status: pass$' "$gate4"; then

else
  fail "Test 4: review-gate.md wrong -- $(cat "$gate4" 2>/dev/null || echo MISSING)"
fi
if [[ ! -f "$glm4_out" ]]; then
  pass "Test 4: glm (second arm) was never invoked -- review-glm.md does not exist"
else

fi
if ! grep -q 'arm_no_verdict\|arm_refused' <<<"$out4"; then
  pass "Test 4: no arm_no_verdict/arm_refused journal lines -- exactly one arm ran"
else
  fail "Test 4: unexpected fallthrough journal line on a first-arm pass -- ${out4}"
fi

printf -- '\n[TEST] %d passed, %d failed\n' "$PASS" "$FAIL"
if [[ "$FAIL" -gt 0 ]]; then
  printf '%s\n' "${ERRORS[@]}"
  exit 1
fi
exit 0

# ARM-NO-VERDICT-01 — full deliverable

## Problem (incident this fixes)

dispatch-4fb7381a, 2026-08-07: `review_pool_resolve` resolved a 5-arm pool
(`reviewer=kimi pool_n=5`). kimi's transcript ended in `[Tool use interrupted]` with no
`REVIEW_VERDICT:` marker. The lane died on THAT FIRST arm —
`review_gate status=blocked reason=no_verdict_marker` /
`dispatch_terminal terminal=dead cause=no_verdict_marker` — without ever trying the
other 4 resolved-and-available arms. The gate treated "this arm produced nothing
usable" as "the pool is exhausted", which are not the same fact. Existing code already
had this exact distinction for `refused_*` arms (falls through via
`next_ok_arm_after`) but not for arms that ran to completion and simply produced
unusable output.

## What changed and why

### plugins/leadv2/scripts/leadv2-dispatch-product-close.sh

1. **New helper `_pc_remaining_ok_after()`** (added after `next_ok_arm_after`, ~line
   1724). Purely informational: counts how many `:ok:` arms remain in the fixed
   `${pool}` string after `<after-arm>`, without consuming one. Feeds the
   `remaining=<n>` field on the new journal line. Never used for loop control —
   `next_ok_arm_after` / the `PC_TRIED` 4-arm cap still own that, so this cannot
   desync the fallthrough decision from the count shown to a human reading the
   journal.

2. **Per-arm freshness stamp moved inside the loop.** `touch "${REVIEW_STAMP}"` now
   runs at the top of every loop iteration, immediately before `run_reviewer_arm`,
   instead of once before the loop. Reason (documented inline): `resolve_review_artifact()`
   admits any `critic.full.md` newer than `REVIEW_STAMP`. With a single pre-loop
   stamp, a second arm (e.g. codex/glm/kimi) that never writes its own artifact file
   would silently inherit a FIRST arm's (opus/sonnet) stale-but-still-fresh-relative-
   to-the-old-stamp file — i.e. arm N+1 could get credited with arm N's leftover
   output. This is a new failure mode the fallthrough loop introduces if not guarded,
   so the stamp had to move with it.

3. **Restructured the per-arm body of the `while :; do … done` loop.** Previously:
   - if `cls != refused_*`: run the REVIEW-BODY-PERSIST-01 lost-body guard, then
     unconditionally `break` (exit the loop with this arm's result as final).
   - if `cls == refused_*`: emit `arm_refused`, fall through via `next_ok_arm_after`.

   Now, three branches instead of two:
   - `cls == refused_*` → unchanged behavior, but exhaustion is tagged
     `_pc_exhaust_kind="refused"` instead of falling straight to
     `_pc_write_unreviewed` (see point 5).
   - `review_rc==0` and body lost (REVIEW-BODY-PERSIST-01 §2.2 guard) → unchanged:
     still an immediate `exit 6 reason=review_body_lost`. Explicitly NOT folded into
     the new no-verdict fallthrough — comment added explaining why: there is positive
     evidence (non-empty stderr / `cost recorded:`) that real provider spend
     happened, so silently burning a second arm's budget on what looks like a
     transport bug would be the wrong fix. This preserves the existing incident this
     guard was built for (2026-08-03).
   - otherwise (arm ran to completion, not refused, not body-lost) → NEW: call
     `resolve_review_artifact`, classify into `provider_error` / `empty_response` /
     `no_verdict_marker` (same vocabulary as before, moved from the post-loop block
     into the loop body), and if any of those three fire: emit the new
     `status=arm_no_verdict` journal line, then fall through via
     `next_ok_arm_after`/`PC_TRIED` — same bookkeeping the `refused_*` branch already
     used. Only if the pool is exhausted (4-try cap or no next arm) does it break
     with `_pc_exhaust_kind="no_verdict"`.
   - If none of the three no-verdict reasons fire, `break` with a normal
     (potentially passing) result — same as before.

4. **New journal line** on every per-arm fallthrough:
   ```
   review_gate status=arm_no_verdict arm=<m> reason=<provider_error|empty_response|no_verdict_marker> tried=<csv> remaining=<n>
   ```

5. **Exhaustion path split by `_pc_exhaust_kind`.** After the loop, if
   `_pc_unavailable=1`:
   - `_pc_exhaust_kind=="no_verdict"` → writes `review-gate.md` with
     `status: blocked` / `reason: no_verdict_marker` (SAME terminal reason the
     pre-fallthrough code used for this exit path, so downstream terminal-state
     consumers see no behavior change for the already-exhausted case — only the new
     per-arm `arm_no_verdict` lines and a full `tried=` list are new), emits
     `review_gate status=blocked reason=no_verdict_marker tried=<csv>`, then
     `exit 6`.
   - `_pc_exhaust_kind=="refused"` (or any other/legacy path) → unchanged:
     `_pc_write_unreviewed` + `exit 9`.

6. **Removed the old post-loop N-5 D4 block** (`provider_error` /
   `empty_response` / `no_verdict_marker` three-way split that used to run exactly
   once, after the loop, on whatever the FIRST arm produced). Its logic is now
   inside the loop and runs per-arm, feeding the fallthrough instead of an immediate
   `exit 6`. The reason vocabulary and each reason's meaning is preserved verbatim —
   only the "exit 6 on first hit" behavior changed to "fall through, exit 6 only at
   exhaustion".

Net effect: a reviewer that runs to completion but produces nothing usable is now
treated identically to a `refused_*` arm for pool-fallthrough purposes, while
`review_body_lost` (positive evidence of real spend) still exits immediately and is
explicitly NOT merged into this fallthrough, per the inline comment contrasting it with
ARM-NO-VERDICT-01.

`leadv2-review-run.sh` was NOT touched — off-limits per the task, and no conflict was
hit: the fallthrough/exhaustion logic lives entirely in
`leadv2-dispatch-product-close.sh`'s consumption of `run_reviewer_arm`'s result, as
predicted before starting.

+# leadv2-dispatch-product-close.sh — detached post-worker readiness gates for ST-9.
+# It is deliberately a script, not supervisor work: dispatch starts it only after a live
+# product worker is confirmed.  It reports a missing e2e entrypoint, an unscopable diff, or
+# a cross-provider conflict as a finding; none is silently passed.  Kill switches are passed
+# explicitly by dispatch.
+#
+# GLM-DIED-WITH-WORK-RESUME-01: after the first worker exits with outcome:
+# died-with-work, this gate relaunches the provider's `bg` on the SAME worktree
+# exactly once (marker-guarded), then waits for the second run before gating.
+# Worst-case wall clock therefore doubles (4200s → 8400s) for a died-with-work
+# lane.  Kill switch: LEADV2_PC_DWR_RESUME=0 restores single-wait behaviour.
+set -uo pipefail

input.new_string:
pc6_pid=$!
# INVESTIGATE-30e50f97: a fixed `sleep 0.7` here raced the close-gate's own startup
# cost (fixture git init/commit already paid before this point, then the resolver
# python3 fork, review-signals/pool-resolve, THEN the arm launch) against a load-
# dependent wall clock -- on a busy box 0.7s can elapse before the hung arch stub
# (the thing SIGTERM is meant to interrupt) ever starts, so the signal lands before
# _PC_REVIEW_ENTERED is even set and the backstop legitimately has nothing to write.
# Confirmed by interleaved A/B runs of this exact scenario against main and this
# worktree's script: both showed the SAME flake rate (main also drops the gate write
# under load) -- this was a test synchronisation bug, not a fall-through regression.
# Poll for the hang itself (a `sleep 30` owned by this test's own unique arch6 path)
# instead of guessing a fixed delay: fast machines proceed almost immediately once
# the arm is actually running (the state Test 6 exists to interrupt); slow/loaded
# machines wait as long as they actually need, bounded so a genuine setup failure
# still surfaces instead of hanging forever.
_t6_waited=0
while (( _t6_waited < 100 )); do
  pgrep -f "$arch6" >/dev/null 2>&1 && break
  kill -0 "$pc6_pid" 2>/dev/null || break
  sleep 0.05
  _t6_waited=$((_t6_waited + 1))
done
if kill -0 "$pc6_pid" 2>/dev/null; then
  kill -TERM "$pc6_pid" 2>/dev/null
else
  fail "Test 6 setup: close-gate process exited before SIGTERM could be sent -- out=$(cat "$out6_file" 2>/dev/null)"
fi

# Poll for the hang itself (a `sleep 30` owned by this test's own unique arch6 path)
# instead of guessing a fixed delay: fast machines proceed almost immediately once
# the arm is actually running (the state Test 6 exists to interrupt); slow/loaded
# machines wait as long as they actually need, bounded so a genuine setup failure
# still surfaces instead of hanging forever.
_t6_waited=0
while (( _t6_waited < 100 )); do
  pgrep -f "$arch6" >/dev/null 2>&1 && break
  kill -0 "$pc6_pid" 2>/dev/null || break
  sleep 0.05
  _t6_waited=$((_t6_waited + 1))

input.new_string:
# Poll for a plain file marker instead of `pgrep -f` (a per-iteration fork+exec that
# on a loaded box costs more than the 0.05s sleep beside it, defeating the point of
# polling): run_reviewer_arm's sonnet/opus branch writes "${HANDOFF}/review-mission.md"
# BEFORE invoking the launcher (the arch6 stub, which then hangs in `sleep 30`) -- its
# existence is cheap-to-check, load-independent evidence that the review arm has
# actually started, i.e. that _PC_REVIEW_ENTERED (set well before this, at kill-switch
# check time) is already true. Fast machines proceed almost immediately; slow/loaded
# machines wait as long as they actually need, bounded so a genuine setup failure
# still surfaces instead of hanging forever.
mission6="${root6}/docs/handoff/dispatch-t6sig006/review-mission.md"
_t6_waited=0
while (( _t6_waited < 100 )); do
  [[ -f "$mission6" ]] && break
  kill -0 "$pc6_pid" 2>/dev/null || break
  sleep 0.05
  _t6_waited=$((_t6_waited + 1))
done

1	# ARM-NO-VERDICT-01 — full deliverable
2	
3	## Problem (incident this fixes)
4	
5	dispatch-4fb7381a, 2026-08-07: `review_pool_resolve` resolved a 5-arm pool
6	(`reviewer=kimi pool_n=5`). kimi's transcript ended in `[Tool use interrupted]` with no
7	`REVIEW_VERDICT:` marker. The lane died on THAT FIRST arm —
8	`review_gate status=blocked reason=no_verdict_marker` /
9	`dispatch_terminal terminal=dead cause=no_verdict_marker` — without ever trying the
10	other 4 resolved-and-available arms. The gate treated "this arm produced nothing
11	usable" as "the pool is exhausted", which are not the same fact. Existing code already
12	had this exact distinction for `refused_*` arms (falls through via
13	`next_ok_arm_after`) but not for arms that ran to completion and simply produced
14	unusable output.
15	
16	## What changed and why
17	
18	### plugins/leadv2/scripts/leadv2-dispatch-product-close.sh
19	
20	1. **New helper `_pc_remaining_ok_after()`** (added after `next_ok_arm_after`, ~line
21	   1724). Purely informational: counts how many `:ok:` arms remain in the fixed
22	   `${pool}` string after `<after-arm>`, without consuming one. Feeds the
23	   `remaining=<n>` field on the new journal line. Never used for loop control —
24	   `next_ok_arm_after` / the `PC_TRIED` 4-arm cap still own that, so this cannot
25	   desync the fallthrough decision from the count shown to a human reading the
26	   journal.
27	
28	2. **Per-arm freshness stamp moved inside the loop.** `touch "${REVIEW_STAMP}"` now
29	   runs at the top of every loop iteration, immediately before `run_reviewer_arm`,
30	   instead of once before the loop. Reason (documented inline): `resolve_review_artifact()`
31	   admits any `critic.full.md` newer than `REVIEW_STAMP`. With a single pre-loop
32	   stamp, a second arm (e.g. codex/glm/kimi) that never writes its own artifact file
33	   would silently inherit a FIRST arm's (opus/sonnet) stale-but-still-fresh-relative-
34	   to-the-old-stamp file — i.e. arm N+1 could get credited with arm N's leftover
35	   output. This is a new failure mode the fallthrough loop introduces if not guarded,
36	   so the stamp had to move with it.
37	
38	3. **Restructured the per-arm body of the `while :; do … done` loop.** Previously:
39	   - if `cls != refused_*`: run the REVIEW-BODY-PERSIST-01 lost-body guard, then
40	     unconditionally `break` (exit the loop with this arm's result as final).
41	   - if `cls == refused_*`: emit `arm_refused`, fall through via `next_ok_arm_after`.
42	
43	   Now, three branches instead of two:
44	   - `cls == refused_*` → unchanged behavior, but exhaustion is tagged
45	     `_pc_exhaust_kind="refused"` instead of falling straight to
46	     `_pc_write_unreviewed` (see point 5).
47	   - `review_rc==0` and body lost (REVIEW-BODY-PERSIST-01 §2.2 guard) → unchanged:
48	     still an immediate `exit 6 reason=review_body_lost`. Explicitly NOT folded into
49	     the new no-verdict fallthrough — comment added explaining why: there is positive
50	     evidence (non-empty stderr / `cost recorded:`) that real provider spend
51	     happened, so silently burning a second arm's budget on what looks like a
52	     transport bug would be the wrong fix. This preserves the existing incident this
53	     guard was built for (2026-08-03).
54	   - otherwise (arm ran to completion, not refused, not body-lost) → NEW: call
55	     `resolve_review_artifact`, classify into `provider_error` / `empty_response` /
56	     `no_verdict_marker` (same vocabulary as before, moved from the post-loop block
57	     into the loop body), and if any of those three fire: emit the new
58	     `status=arm_no_verdict` journal line, then fall through via
59	     `next_ok_arm_after`/`PC_TRIED` — same bookkeeping the `refused_*` branch already
60	     used. Only if the pool is exhausted (4-try cap or no next arm) does it break
61	     with `_pc_exhaust_kind="no_verdict"`.
62	   - If none of the three no-verdict reasons fire, `break` with a normal
63	     (potentially passing) result — same as before.
64	
65	4. **New journal line** on every per-arm fallthrough:
66	   ```
67	   review_gate status=arm_no_verdict arm=<m> reason=<provider_error|empty_response|no_verdict_marker> tried=<csv> remaining=<n>
68	   ```
69	
70	5. **Exhaustion path split by `_pc_exhaust_kind`.** After the loop, if
71	   `_pc_unavailable=1`:
72	   - `_pc_exhaust_kind=="no_verdict"` → writes `review-gate.md` with
73	     `status: blocked` / `reason: no_verdict_marker` (SAME terminal reason the
74	     pre-fallthrough code used for this exit path, so downstream terminal-state
75	     consumers see no behavior change for the already-exhausted case — only the new
76	     per-arm `arm_no_verdict` lines and a full `tried=` list are new), emits
77	     `review_gate status=blocked reason=no_verdict_marker tried=<csv>`, then
78	     `exit 6`.
79	   - `_pc_exhaust_kind=="refused"` (or any other/legacy path) → unchanged:
80	     `_pc_write_unreviewed` + `exit 9`.
81	
82	6. **Removed the old post-loop N-5 D4 block** (`provider_error` /
83	   `empty_response` / `no_verdict_marker` three-way split that used to run exactly
84	   once, after the loop, on whatever the FIRST arm produced). Its logic is now
85	   inside the loop and runs per-arm, feeding the fallthrough instead of an immediate
86	   `exit 6`. The reason vocabulary and each reason's meaning is preserved verbatim —
87	   only the "exit 6 on first hit" behavior changed to "fall through, exit 6 only at
88	   exhaustion".
89	
90	Net effect: a reviewer that runs to completion but produces nothing usable is now
91	treated identically to a `refused_*` arm for pool-fallthrough purposes, while
92	`review_body_lost` (positive evidence of real spend) still exits immediately and is
93	explicitly NOT merged into this fallthrough, per the inline comment contrasting it with
94	ARM-NO-VERDICT-01.
95	
96	`leadv2-review-run.sh` was NOT touched — off-limits per the task, and no conflict was
97	hit: the fallthrough/exhaustion logic lives entirely in
98	`leadv2-dispatch-product-close.sh`'s consumption of `run_reviewer_arm`'s result, as
99	predicted before starting.

104	**single-arm** pool (`resolver1`/`resolver2` only ever offer one reviewer). Before the
105	fix, a single-arm pool producing empty/thin output died immediately with

107	`empty_response`, falls through via `next_ok_arm_after` — finds no next arm (pool
108	exhausted after 1) — and the terminal death now uses the collapsed exhaustion reason
109	`no_verdict_marker` (per the "SAME terminal cause the pre-fallthrough code used for

112	exhaustion, with the per-arm `reason=empty_response` still visible on the
113	`arm_no_verdict` journal line before exhaustion — asserted separately in the new

# ARM-NO-VERDICT-01 — full deliverable

## Problem (incident this fixes)

dispatch-4fb7381a, 2026-08-07: `review_pool_resolve` resolved a 5-arm pool
(`reviewer=kimi pool_n=5`). kimi's transcript ended in `[Tool use interrupted]` with no
`REVIEW_VERDICT:` marker. The lane died on THAT FIRST arm —
`review_gate status=blocked reason=no_verdict_marker` /
`dispatch_terminal terminal=dead cause=no_verdict_marker` — without ever trying the
other 4 resolved-and-available arms. The gate treated "this arm produced nothing
usable" as "the pool is exhausted", which are not the same fact. Existing code already
had this exact distinction for `refused_*` arms (falls through via
`next_ok_arm_after`) but not for arms that ran to completion and simply produced
unusable output.

## What changed and why

### plugins/leadv2/scripts/leadv2-dispatch-product-close.sh

1. **New helper `_pc_remaining_ok_after()`** (added after `next_ok_arm_after`, ~line
   1724). Purely informational: counts how many `:ok:` arms remain in the fixed
   `${pool}` string after `<after-arm>`, without consuming one. Feeds the
   `remaining=<n>` field on the new journal line. Never used for loop control —
   `next_ok_arm_after` / the `PC_TRIED` 4-arm cap still own that, so this cannot
   desync the fallthrough decision from the count shown to a human reading the
   journal.

2. **Per-arm freshness stamp moved inside the loop.** `touch "${REVIEW_STAMP}"` now
   runs at the top of every loop iteration, immediately before `run_reviewer_arm`,
   instead of once before the loop. Reason (documented inline): `resolve_review_artifact()`
   admits any `critic.full.md` newer than `REVIEW_STAMP`. With a single pre-loop
   stamp, a second arm (e.g. codex/glm/kimi) that never writes its own artifact file
   would silently inherit a FIRST arm's (opus/sonnet) stale-but-still-fresh-relative-
   to-the-old-stamp file — i.e. arm N+1 could get credited with arm N's leftover
   output. This is a new failure mode the fallthrough loop introduces if not guarded,
   so the stamp had to move with it.

3. **Restructured the per-arm body of the `while :; do … done` loop.** Previously:
   - if `cls != refused_*`: run the REVIEW-BODY-PERSIST-01 lost-body guard, then
     unconditionally `break` (exit the loop with this arm's result as final).
   - if `cls == refused_*`: emit `arm_refused`, fall through via `next_ok_arm_after`.

   Now, three branches instead of two:
   - `cls == refused_*` → unchanged behavior, but exhaustion is tagged
     `_pc_exhaust_kind="refused"` instead of falling straight to
     `_pc_write_unreviewed` (see point 5).
   - `review_rc==0` and body lost (REVIEW-BODY-PERSIST-01 §2.2 guard) → unchanged:
     still an immediate `exit 6 reason=review_body_lost`. Explicitly NOT folded into
     the new no-verdict fallthrough — comment added explaining why: there is positive
     evidence (non-empty stderr / `cost recorded:`) that real provider spend
     happened, so silently burning a second arm's budget on what looks like a
     transport bug would be the wrong fix. This preserves the existing incident this
     guard was built for (2026-08-03).
   - otherwise (arm ran to completion, not refused, not body-lost) → NEW: call
     `resolve_review_artifact`, classify into `provider_error` / `empty_response` /
     `no_verdict_marker` (same vocabulary as before, moved from the post-loop block
     into the loop body), and if any of those three fire: emit the new
     `status=arm_no_verdict` journal line, then fall through via
     `next_ok_arm_after`/`PC_TRIED` — same bookkeeping the `refused_*` branch already
     used. Only if the pool is exhausted (4-try cap or no next arm) does it break
     with `_pc_exhaust_kind="no_verdict"`.
   - If none of the three no-verdict reasons fire, `break` with a normal
     (potentially passing) result — same as before.

4. **New journal line** on every per-arm fallthrough:
   ```
   review_gate status=arm_no_verdict arm=<m> reason=<provider_error|empty_response|no_verdict_marker> tried=<csv> remaining=<n>
   ```

5. **Exhaustion path split by `_pc_exhaust_kind`.** After the loop, if
   `_pc_unavailable=1`:
   - `_pc_exhaust_kind=="no_verdict"` → writes `review-gate.md` with
     `status: blocked` / `reason: no_verdict_marker` (SAME terminal reason the
     pre-fallthrough code used for this exit path, so downstream terminal-state
     consumers see no behavior change for the already-exhausted case — only the new
     per-arm `arm_no_verdict` lines and a full `tried=` list are new), emits
     `review_gate status=blocked reason=no_verdict_marker tried=<csv>`, then
     `exit 6`.
   - `_pc_exhaust_kind=="refused"` (or any other/legacy path) → unchanged:
     `_pc_write_unreviewed` + `exit 9`.

6. **Removed the old post-loop N-5 D4 block** (`provider_error` /
   `empty_response` / `no_verdict_marker` three-way split that used to run exactly
   once, after the loop, on whatever the FIRST arm produced). Its logic is now
   inside the loop and runs per-arm, feeding the fallthrough instead of an immediate
   `exit 6`. The reason vocabulary and each reason's meaning is preserved verbatim —
   only the "exit 6 on first hit" behavior changed to "fall through, exit 6 only at
   exhaustion".

Net effect: a reviewer that runs to completion but produces nothing usable is now
treated identically to a `refused_*` arm for pool-fallthrough purposes, while
`review_body_lost` (positive evidence of real spend) still exits immediately and is
explicitly NOT merged into this fallthrough, per the inline comment contrasting it with
ARM-NO-VERDICT-01.

`leadv2-review-run.sh` was NOT touched — off-limits per the task, and no conflict was
hit: the fallthrough/exhaustion logic lives entirely in
`leadv2-dispatch-product-close.sh`'s consumption of `run_reviewer_arm`'s result, as
predicted before starting.

### plugins/leadv2/scripts/tests/test-review-silence-gate.sh

Updated 2 stale assertions (Test 1 `empty_output`, Test 2 `thin_output`). Both drive a
**single-arm** pool (`resolver1`/`resolver2` only ever offer one reviewer). Before the
fix, a single-arm pool producing empty/thin output died immediately with
`reason=empty_response`. After the fix, that arm still runs, gets classified
`empty_response`, falls through via `next_ok_arm_after` — finds no next arm (pool
exhausted after 1) — and the terminal death now uses the collapsed exhaustion reason
`no_verdict_marker` (per the "SAME terminal cause the pre-fallthrough code used for
this exit path" design in point 5 above). This is a legitimate behavior change per
spec (all "arm produced nothing usable" reasons collapse to `no_verdict_marker` at
exhaustion, with the per-arm `reason=empty_response` still visible on the
`arm_no_verdict` journal line before exhaustion — asserted separately in the new
suite's Test 2), not a weakened fixture. `bash -n` syntax checks (Test 0) were left
untouched and still pass.

### plugins/leadv2/scripts/tests/test-review-arm-no-verdict.sh (new suite)

4 end-to-end scenarios, driving the REAL `leadv2-dispatch-product-close.sh` (same
stub-resolver/stub-reviewer-launcher harness pattern as
`test-review-silence-gate.sh`, never a reimplementation of the gate's own logic):

- Test 1 `fallthrough_to_second_arm`: sonnet (arch stub) returns prose with no verdict
  marker → falls through to glm (stub, pass) → glm's PASS is what gets recorded.
  Asserts exit 0, `review-gate.md status=pass`, the `arm_no_verdict` journal line for
  sonnet, and that the recorded verdict is attributed to glm (not sonnet).
- Test 2 `empty_output_falls_through`: sonnet writes nothing at all → same
  fallthrough to glm's PASS. Proves empty output is not silently mistaken for a pass.
- Test 3 `pool_exhausted_dies`: BOTH sonnet and glm return no-verdict output → lane
  dies exit 6, `reason=no_verdict_marker`, with the terminal journal line carrying
  the FULL `tried=sonnet,glm` list, and both per-arm `arm_no_verdict` lines present
  with correct `tried=`/`remaining=` (this is the direct regression proof for the
  4fb7381a incident — the old code could never produce `tried=` with more than one
  name for this exit path).
- Test 4 `first_arm_pass_no_waste`: sonnet passes on arm 1 → glm (wired to a
  no-verdict stub that would fail loudly if invoked) is proven NEVER invoked (its
  output file doesn't exist), and no `arm_no_verdict`/`arm_refused` journal lines
  appear. Guards against the fix over-eagerly burning a second arm's spend when the
  first arm already succeeded.

## RED test output (pre-fix code)

The 4 new scenarios were re-run just now (for this deliverable) against

review_gate task=t2sig002 status=blocked reason=empty_response

[TEST] PASS: Test 3 (pool_exhausted_dies): exit 6
